_meta.scope: Wiring 8 AAWSAP/AATIP Defense Intelligence Reference Documents (DIRDs) out of the dird-series hub by establishing author, affiliation, DIA document number, publication date and Intelligence Cut-Off Date for each.
_meta.authority: DIA letter to the Senate Armed Services Committee (offices of Sen. John McCain and Sen. Jack Reed), transmitting a list of all 38 products produced under the AATIP/AAWSAP contract. Provided to Congress January 2018; released under FOIA to Steven Aftergood (Federation of American Scientists) 16 January 2019 and posted at irp.fas.org/dia/aatip-list.pdf. Every author attribution below is taken from that list and, where the DIRD itself has been released, cross-checked against the cover page (title, series, publication date, ICOD, DIA document number).
_meta.method: The FAS/DIA list PDF is a scan and does not yield machine text. The list was read from two independent transcriptions that distinguish the DIA/FAS list from the earlier (July 2018) George Knapp / KLAS-TV list, and from The Black Vault's DIRD archive page which reproduces the DIA list entries alongside the released PDFs. Cover-page data was read from the released PDFs themselves as mirrored by The Black Vault. Author names on the released PDF cover pages are redacted under (b)(6) / (b)(3):10 USC 424, so authorship rests on the DIA list, not on the PDFs.
_meta.notes: All eight DIRDs in this batch have been released in redacted form. The author name is redacted on every released cover page; the DIA congressional list is the only authoritative naming source.

people.label: George D. Hathaway
people.sub: Professional engineer, Hathaway Consulting Services (Toronto); author of two AAWSAP DIRDs
people.narrative:
George D. Hathaway is a Canadian professional engineer who graduated from the Department of Electrical Engineering at the University of Toronto in 1974 and built a consulting practice around experimental testing of unconventional energy and propulsion claims. He appears twice by name on the DIA list of AATIP/AAWSAP products transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee, credited as author of item 10, 'Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research', and item 16, 'Maverick Inventor Versus Corporate Inventor: Where Will the Next Major Innovations Arise?', in both cases with the affiliation Hathaway Consulting. That places him among the small group of AAWSAP contributors who produced more than one deliverable.

His self-description, preserved from his now-defunct company site and quoted in The Black Vault's DIRD archive, is that of a hands-on experimentalist rather than a theorist: a consultant on 'novel and exotic materials, energy production and propulsion concepts', an expert on 'experimental design, analysis, testing' and, pointedly, 'an expert on scientific and engineering measurements and their misuse'. He is also a machinist, a reviewer for scientific publications, and author of the book 'Mindbending: The Hutchison Files'.

That last credit is the reason his presence on a Defense Intelligence Agency contract is analytically significant rather than routine. Hathaway's public body of work sits inside the anomalous-physics testing community that Robert Bigelow's ventures drew on, and his Maverick Inventor DIRD is not a physics paper at all but a research-culture argument about whether breakthrough invention comes from lone inventors or corporate laboratories. The Defense Intelligence Reference Document series was defined by DIA as providing 'non-substantive but authoritative reference information'; item 16 shows how loosely that mandate was drawn in practice. His Maverick Inventor DIRD carries DIA document number DIA-08-1003-017, published 30 March 2010 with an ICOD of 1 December 2009, and is identified on its own cover page as one of a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the AAWSA Program.

people.label: Sergey O. Macheret
people.sub: Plasma physicist; senior staff engineer, Lockheed Martin Skunk Works 2006-2014; author, MHD Air Breathing Propulsion DIRD
people.narrative:
Sergey O. Macheret is a Ukrainian-American plasma physicist and aerospace engineer, and he is the single clearest example on the DIRD list of a mainstream, credentialled defence-industry scientist being drawn into the AAWSAP deliverable stream. He took an M.S. in physics from the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology and a Ph.D. in plasma physics and plasma chemistry from the Kurchatov Institute, emigrated to the United States in 1991, and held research posts at Ohio State and Princeton before joining Lockheed Martin Aeronautics.

The DIA list transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee credits him as author of 'Magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications' with the affiliation Lockheed Martin. That affiliation is exact for the period: he was a senior staff engineer at Lockheed Martin Skunk Works from 2006 to 2014, which brackets the document's 21 November 2010 publication date and its 20 July 2010 Intelligence Cut-Off Date. He left for Purdue University in 2014 as a professor of aeronautics and astronautics, added a professorship in electrical and computer engineering in 2022, was elected an AIAA Fellow, received the AIAA Plasmadynamics and Lasers Award in 2022, and founded US Plasma Engineering LLC in 2023.

His DIRD is one of three Lockheed Martin products on the DIA list and reads as ordinary hypersonics work rather than fringe physics: MHD control of ionised flow around an air-breathing vehicle, with explicit reference to Soviet work on the Ajax (Ayaks) hypersonic concept associated with the Leninets Design Bureau in St. Petersburg. That is squarely within the stated AAWSAP purpose of assessing foreign advanced aerospace weapon threats out to forty years, and it is the strongest available counterweight to the assumption that the DIRD series was uniformly speculative. Macheret has no public association with UAP research, with Bigelow's organisations, or with the anomalous-physics network that produced the EarthTech deliverables; his presence on the list is best read as a contracted subject-matter survey by a working plasma dynamicist.

people.label: Friedwardt Winterberg
people.sub: Theoretical physicist, research professor, University of Nevada, Reno; author of two AAWSAP DIRDs
people.narrative:
Friedwardt Winterberg is a German-American theoretical physicist and research professor at the University of Nevada, Reno, with a long publication record spanning general relativity, Planck-scale physics, nuclear fusion and plasma physics. He appears twice on the DIA list of AATIP/AAWSAP products transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee: as author of item 2, 'Advanced Nuclear Propulsion for Manned Deep Space Missions', and as author of 'Negative Mass Propulsion', both with the affiliation University of Nevada, Reno.

His geographic placement matters to the shape of the programme. AAWSAP funding was directed by Senator Harry Reid toward a Nevada constituent, and the DIRD author list carries an unusually heavy Nevada concentration — Winterberg at UNR, and separate deliverables credited to the University of Nevada, Las Vegas. Winterberg is the only author on the list credited with two Nevada-institution papers, and both of his are propulsion physics rather than the anomalous-phenomena material that dominates the EarthTech contributions.

'Negative Mass Propulsion' carries DIA document number DIA-08-1101-023, published 3 January 2011 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 30 August 2010, in the 'Defense Futures' series, and its cover page identifies it as one of a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2010 under the AAWSA Program. The subject is the classic Bondi problem of runaway motion between positive and negative gravitational mass, considered as a propulsion concept: a vehicle accelerating without expelling reaction mass. Winterberg published closely related work in the peer-reviewed literature, which distinguishes his DIRD from several others on the list that have no independent scholarly footprint. The document was released by DIA under FOIA and posted to the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room; the author name is redacted on the released cover page under (b)(6), so the attribution rests on the congressional list rather than on the document itself.

people.label: Gerald A. Smith
people.sub: Experimental particle physicist; Professor Emeritus, Penn State; founder, Positronics Research LLC (New Mexico)
people.narrative:
Gerald A. Smith is an experimental high-energy physicist with an unusually deep institutional pedigree who ended his career building antimatter storage hardware for NASA and then selling antimatter propulsion concepts through a small New Mexico company. He is credited on the DIA list of AATIP/AAWSAP products transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee as author of 'Positron Aerospace Propulsion', affiliation Positronics Research.

His background: B.A. in physics from Miami University (Ohio) in 1957, M.S. (1958) and Ph.D. (1961) in physics from Yale, a second-generation graduate student of Enrico Fermi, and post-doctoral years from 1961 to 1966 as an assistant professor under Luis Alvarez at Berkeley. He built a high-energy physics programme at Michigan State from 1968, served as Associate Laboratory Director for High Energy Physics at Argonne in 1978, and in 1983 became Director of the Laboratory for Elementary Particle Science and Physics Department Head at Penn State. He was spokesperson for international collaborations at Brookhaven, CERN, Fermilab and SLAC, has more than 300 refereed publications, and is a Fellow of the American Physical Society. At Penn State he oversaw the ICAN-II and AIMStar antimatter-catalysed designs and the development of two antiproton traps: the Mark I portable trap for JPL and the High Performance Antimatter Trap (HiPAT) for NASA Marshall. He became Professor Emeritus in 2000 and founded Positronics Research LLC in 2001.

His DIRD is therefore a case where AAWSAP bought a survey from a genuine domain authority, and it aligns with work he was already doing publicly: his positron-propelled vehicle concept was a NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts Phase I study and was written up by NASA in 2006. The AAWSAP deliverable carries DIA document number DIA-08-1003-002, published 2 March 2010 with an ICOD of 1 December 2009, in the 'Acquisition Threat Support' series. It is one of the DIRDs released by DIA in redacted form; the author line on the released cover page is blanked.

claims.text: Named on the DIA list of AATIP/AAWSAP products supplied to the Senate Armed Services Committee as author of 'Positron Aerospace Propulsion', affiliation Positronics Research.

Oversaw development of the Mark I portable antiproton trap for NASA JPL and the High Performance Antimatter Trap (HiPAT) for NASA Marshall; principal investigator on a NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts Phase I study, 'Positron Propelled and Powered Space Transport Vehicle for Planetary Missions'.

people.label: James Wells
people.sub: Author, Pulsed High-Power Microwave Source Technology DIRD; affiliation given as J W Enterprises on the DIA list
people.narrative:
James Wells is credited on the DIA list of AATIP/AAWSAP products transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee as author of 'Pulsed High-Power Microwave Technology'. He is one of the least publicly traceable names on the list, and he is also the one clear instance in this batch where the two circulating versions of the DIRD roster disagree on affiliation.

The DIA list released to the Federation of American Scientists in January 2019 gives his affiliation as 'J W Enterprises'. The earlier list published by George Knapp and Matt Adams of KLAS-TV on 25 July 2018 — a near-complete roster whose authenticity was confirmed by former programme manager Luis Elizondo, but whose source was never disclosed — gives his affiliation as 'Northrop Grumman'. The DIA list is the authoritative document because it was prepared by the agency and transmitted to Congress; 'J W Enterprises' is therefore recorded here as the affiliation of record, with the Northrop Grumman variant preserved as a discrepancy rather than discarded. The two are not necessarily contradictory in substance — a named consultancy and a prime contractor could both be true of the same person at different points — but nothing sourced resolves it, and the difference should not be smoothed over.

Beyond the list entry itself, no verified biography, institutional page or publication record has been located for him, and the released DIRD does not help: the author line on the cover page is redacted under (b)(6). What is firmly established is the document. 'Pulsed High-Power Microwave Source Technology' carries DIA document number DIA-08-0912-005, published 28 January 2010 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 1 December 2009, in the 'Acquisition Threat Support' series. It runs 37 pages and was released by DIA in redacted form. Its subject — directed-energy source hardware — is among the most conventionally military topics in the entire series.

people.label: Richard J. Genik II
people.sub: Director, Emergent Technology Research Division, and assistant professor of psychiatry and behavioral neurosciences, Wayne State University School of Medicine
people.narrative:
Richard J. Genik II is director of the Emergent Technology Research Division and an assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences at the Wayne State University School of Medicine. He is one of the more prolific AAWSAP contributors, credited on the DIA list transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee with 'Quantum Computing and Utilizing Organic Molecules in Automation Technology' and, elsewhere on the same list, with item 20, 'Technological Approaches to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces' — brain-machine interface work squarely within his stated speciality.

His Wayne State affiliation is the significant structural fact. Wayne State is also the affiliation given on the DIA list for Christopher 'Kit' Green, the former CIA analyst and physician who authored item 12 on human biological field effects and who is one of the central figures in the legacy-programme narrative. Two of the 38 DIRDs are therefore credited to a single medical school, and the human-effects and human-interface strands of the AAWSAP deliverable set both run through it. Genik has also been publicly identified as one of fifteen experts selected by the U.S. Army to advise on how the service should direct its neuroscience research funding over the following two decades, which places him in the applied military-neuroscience advisory community independently of AAWSAP.

His quantum computing DIRD sits oddly against that background — it is a survey of quantum information substrates including organic molecules, quantum dots and graphene, not a neuroscience paper. It carries DIA document number DIA-08-1102-005, published 10 December 2010, in the 'Defense Futures' series, and it is one of the few DIRDs whose Intelligence Cut-Off Date is identical to its publication date, also 10 December 2010, meaning it was issued with no lag between research cutoff and release. The released copy is redacted; the author line is blanked, and the attribution rests on the congressional list.

Hathaway is also credited on the same list with 'Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research'. The author line on the released PDF is redacted under (b)(6).

edges.label: produced under the AAWSA/AAWSAP contract, FY 2009
edges.note: The document's administrative note states it is 'one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program'. Issued as DIA-08-1003-017 on 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009. It is not a physics paper: it is a research-culture argument about whether breakthrough invention originates with lone inventors or corporate laboratories, which is the clearest single illustration of how loosely the DIRD mandate was drawn in practice.

edges.label: commissioned via the BAASS prime contract
edges.note: Hathaway Consulting was a one-man Toronto engineering consultancy with no independent DIA relationship; its deliverable reached DIA through the AAWSAP prime contract held by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies. Tier 2 because the contractor name is redacted on the cover page under (b)(3):10 USC 424 and the subcontract has not been released. Reporting has separately characterised Hathaway as having ties to Bigelow's fringe and paranormal research interests, but no primary document establishing an employment or advisory relationship has been located.

edges.label: senior staff engineer, Lockheed Martin Aeronautics (Skunk Works)
edges.note: Macheret held a senior staff engineer post at Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company, Skunk Works, from 2006 to 2014, working on advanced aerospace plasma applications, before joining Purdue University as professor of aeronautics and astronautics in 2014. Lockheed Martin is the affiliation DIA recorded for him on the congressional list.

edges.label: director, Emergent Technology Research Division; assistant professor of psychiatry and behavioral neurosciences
edges.note: Wayne State University School of Medicine identifies Genik as director of its Emergent Technology Research Division and an assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences. Wayne State is the affiliation DIA recorded for him on the congressional list. The dateStart is the date of the university announcement establishing the role, not necessarily the start of his tenure.

edges.label: co-affiliated AAWSAP authors at Wayne State University
edges.note: The DIA congressional list records Wayne State University as the affiliation for both Genik's deliverables and for Kit Green's human biological tissue field-effects deliverable. This establishes a documented shared institutional affiliation on the same contract, not a documented working relationship — no primary source describing collaboration between them has been located, and the edge should not be read as one.

unresolved: No subject-domain node exists on the board for the domains these eight documents actually occupy. The only domain node offered was d-materials, which fits none of them. Recommend adding d-propulsion (would take negative-mass, positron, laser-lightcraft, MHD), d-directed-energy (pulsed high-power microwave, laser-lightcraft) and d-quantum (quantum tomography, quantum computing) before the next DIRD batch, otherwise the subject-domain leg of the wiring cannot be completed for most of the series.

james-wells affiliation conflict, unresolved: the DIA list released to FAS gives 'J W Enterprises'; the earlier George Knapp / KLAS-TV roster of 25 July 2018 gives 'Northrop Grumman'. Both rosters are otherwise substantially consistent, and Elizondo confirmed the Knapp roster genuine. The DIA list is recorded as authoritative here. Resolution would require the FOIA-released contract or subcontract paperwork naming the DIRD authors, which has not been released.

No institution node exists for Hathaway Consulting (Toronto), Positronics Research LLC (New Mexico), J W Enterprises, or the University of Nevada, Reno. Four of the eight documents therefore have no employer-institution edge and were given a baass funding edge in its place. Adding university-nevada-reno in particular would be worthwhile: it would also pick up Winterberg's second DIRD and sits directly on the Reid/Nevada funding axis.

Author names are redacted under (b)(6) and (b)(3):10 USC 424 on every released DIRD cover page in this batch, without exception. Every author attribution here therefore rests entirely on the DIA congressional list. No cover page independently corroborates an author name. This is a systemic single-source condition across the whole DIRD series and should be flagged on the board rather than left implicit.

george-hathaway's relationship to Bigelow's organisations is asserted in reporting (TWZ describes him as 'another person with clear ties to Bigelow and his more fringe and paranormal interests') but no primary document establishing employment, subcontract or advisory board membership with NIDS, Bigelow Aerospace or BAASS has been located. No nids or bigelow edge was written for him. If a NIDS science advisory board roster surfaces, that is the edge to add.

The DIA list PDF at irp.fas.org/dia/aatip-list.pdf is a five-page scan that yields no machine-readable text through the available fetch tooling. Its contents were read here through two independent transcriptions that explicitly distinguish the DIA/FAS list from the earlier Knapp list, cross-checked against The Black Vault's DIRD archive page. A human verification pass against the scanned images themselves is advisable before these attributions are treated as final.
Item 38 on the DIA list is redacted in full. It is not among this batch, but it means the board's dird-series can never be fully enumerated from the congressional list alone.
